question: Which part of the Indian Constitution is mentioned as 'Magna Carta of India'? (RPF Constable 2018 (11/02/2019))
options: Part 2
Part 3
Part 1
Part 4
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Part 3

Explanation:
Part 3 (Articles 12-35) of the Indian Constitution deals with Fundamental Rights. It is called the Magna Carta of India because it guarantees six fundamental rights to citizens: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies. The Magna Carta (1215) was a British charter that limited the king's powers and laid the foundation of individual liberty. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called Fundamental Rights the heart of the Constitution. Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to enforce these rights. Originally, there were seven fundamental rights, but the Right to Property (Article 31) was removed by the 44th Amendment, 1978.

☛ Which articles cover Fundamental Rights? → Articles 12-35
☛ How many Fundamental Rights were originally in the Constitution? → 7 (now 6)
☛ Which article is called the 'heart and soul of the Constitution'? → Article 32
☛ Who is the protector of Fundamental Rights? → Supreme Court
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के किस भाग को 'भारत का मैग्ना कार्टा' कहा गया है? (RPF Constable 2018 (11/02/2019))
options_hi: भाग 2
भाग 3
भाग 1
भाग 4
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भाग 3

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का भाग 3 (अनुच्छेद 12-35) मौलिक अधिकारों से संबंधित है। इसे भारत का मैग्ना कार्टा कहा जाता है क्योंकि यह नागरिकों को छह मौलिक अधिकार प्रदान करता है: समानता का अधिकार, स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार, शोषण के विरुद्ध अधिकार, धर्म की स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार, सांस्कृतिक और शैक्षिक अधिकार, तथा संवैधानिक उपचारों का अधिकार। मैग्ना कार्टा (1215) ब्रिटिश इतिहास का एक चार्टर था जिसने राजा की शक्तियों को सीमित किया और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता की नींव रखी। डॉ. बी.आर. आंबेडकर ने मौलिक अधिकारों को संविधान की आत्मा बताया। अनुच्छेद 32 के तहत सर्वोच्च न्यायालय इन अधिकारों का संरक्षक है।

question: In which of the following countries did the principle of judicial review develop? (RPF Constable 2018 (11/02/2019))
options: United States
England
China
Japan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is United States

Explanation:
The principle of judicial review developed in the United States. It was established by the Supreme Court in the landmark case Marbury v. Madison (1803). This principle empowers the judiciary to review laws and executive actions for their constitutionality. Chief Justice John Marshall declared that the Constitution is the supreme law of the land, and any law or action inconsistent with it is void. This doctrine became a cornerstone of American democracy and was later adopted by many countries, including India.

☛ Year of Marbury v. Madison case → 1803
☛ Basis of Judicial Review → Supremacy of the Constitution
☛ Source of Judicial Review in India → Articles 13, 32, 226
☛ First constitutional court in the world → U.S. Supreme Court
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किस देश में न्यायिक समीक्षा का सिद्धांत विकसित हुआ? (RPF Constable 2018 (11/02/2019))

इंगलैंड
चीन
जापान
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका

Explanation:
न्यायिक समीक्षा का सिद्धांत संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका में विकसित हुआ। यह सिद्धांत मार्बरी बनाम मैडिसन (1803) मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय द्वारा स्थापित किया गया। इसके तहत न्यायपालिका को कानूनों और कार्यकारी आदेशों की संवैधानिकता की जांच करने का अधिकार प्राप्त हुआ। मुख्य न्यायाधीश जॉन मार्शल ने इस फैसले में कहा कि संविधान सर्वोच्च कानून है और कोई भी कानून या कार्य संविधान के विरुद्ध नहीं हो सकता। यह सिद्धांत अमेरिकी लोकतंत्र की मजबूत नींव बना और बाद में भारत सहित कई देशों ने इसे अपनाया।

question: Which of the following is the article related to the power of issuing the President's Ordinance? (RPF Constable 2018 (11/02/2019))
options: Article 153
Article 143
Article 123
Article 133
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 123

Explanation:
Article 123 of the Indian Constitution confers upon the President the power to issue ordinances. This power can be exercised only when both Houses of Parliament are not in session and immediate action is necessary. An ordinance has the same force and effect as a law passed by Parliament, but it must be approved by Parliament within six weeks of reassembly. Article 143 deals with the President's power to consult the Supreme Court, Article 153 deals with the appointment of Governors, and Article 133 deals with appeals to the Supreme Court from High Courts. Hence, only Article 123 is related to the President's ordinance-making power.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When can the President issue an ordinance? → When Parliament is not in session
☛ What is the maximum duration of an ordinance? → Six weeks after the reassembly of Parliament
☛ Can an ordinance be revoked? → Yes, by Parliament
☛ Under which part of the Constitution is Article 123? → Part V (The Union Executive)
☛ Who has the power to issue ordinances? → The President
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा अनुच्छेद राष्ट्रपति की अध्यादेश जारी करने की शक्ति से संबंधित है? (RPF Constable 2018 (11/02/2019))
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 153
अनुच्छेद 143
अनुच्छेद 123
अनुच्छेद 133
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 123

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 123 राष्ट्रपति को अध्यादेश जारी करने की शक्ति प्रदान करता है। यह शक्ति तब प्रयोग की जाती है जब संसद का सत्र नहीं चल रहा हो और तत्काल कार्रवाई आवश्यक हो। राष्ट्रपति के अध्यादेश का वही प्रभाव होता है जो संसद के कानून का होता है, लेकिन इसे संसद के पुनः सत्र शुरू होने के 6 सप्ताह के भीतर अनुमोदित कराना अनिवार्य है। अनुच्छेद 143 सर्वोच्च न्यायालय से परामर्श से संबंधित है, अनुच्छेद 153 राज्यों के राज्यपालों की नियुक्ति से, और अनुच्छेद 133 उच्च न्यायालयों के निर्णयों के विरुद्ध अपील से जुड़ा है। इस प्रकार अध्यादेश की शक्ति केवल अनुच्छेद 123 में निहित है।

question: Which of the following articles is related to the Finance Commission?  (RPF Constable 2018 (11/02/2019))
options: Article 262
Article 280
Article 244
Article 263
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 280

Explanation:
Article 280 of the Indian Constitution deals with the Finance Commission. It empowers the President to constitute a Finance Commission every five years to make recommendations on the distribution of tax proceeds between the Centre and states, and on state financial conditions. The Finance Commission is a constitutional body formed under Article 280. Its chairman and members are appointed by the President. So far, 15 Finance Commissions have been formed. Other options: Article 262 relates to inter-state river water disputes, Article 244 relates to the administration of scheduled and tribal areas, and Article 263 relates to the Inter-State Council.

☛ Article 262 relates to → Inter-state river water disputes
☛ Article 244 relates to → Administration of scheduled and tribal areas
☛ Article 263 relates to → Inter-State Council
☛ Tenure of Finance Commission → Every five years

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 280 वित्त आयोग से संबंधित है। यह अनुच्छेद राष्ट्रपति को एक वित्त आयोग गठित करने का अधिकार देता है, जो हर पांच वर्ष में केंद्र और राज्यों के बीच करों के वितरण, राज्य वित्तीय स्थिति आदि पर सिफारिशें करता है। वित्त आयोग एक संवैधानिक निकाय है जिसका गठन भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 280 के तहत किया जाता है। इसके अध्यक्ष और सदस्यों की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति द्वारा की जाती है। अब तक 15 वित्त आयोग गठित हो चुके हैं। अन्य विकल्पों की बात करें तो अनुच्छेद 262 अंतर-राज्यीय नदी जल विवादों से, अनुच्छेद 244 अनुसूचित और जनजातीय क्षेत्रों से, और अनुच्छेद 263 अंतर-राज्यीय परिषद से संबंधित है।

question: Which of the following high courts has territorial jurisdiction in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands? (RPF Constable 2018 (11/02/2019))
options: Andhra Pradesh High Court
Delhi High Court
Madras High Court
Calcutta High Court
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Calcutta High Court

Explanation:
The Calcutta High Court has territorial jurisdiction over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. This is established under Article 231 of the Constitution of India. The Calcutta High Court was established in 1862 and is one of the oldest high courts in India. The Andaman and Nicobar Islands is a union territory with its capital at Port Blair. The island group consists of approximately 572 islands. The Calcutta High Court is headquartered in Kolkata, West Bengal.

☛ In which state is the Calcutta High Court located? → West Bengal
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किस उच्च न्यायालय का अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह पर क्षेत्रीय अधिकार क्षेत्र है? (RPF Constable 2018 (11/02/2019))

solution_hi:

Explanation:
अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह पर क्षेत्रीय अधिकार क्षेत्र कलकत्ता उच्च न्यायालय का है। यह भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 231 के तहत स्थापित किया गया है। कलकत्ता उच्च न्यायालय की स्थापना 1862 में हुई थी और यह भारत के सबसे पुराने उच्च न्यायालयों में से एक है। अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह एक केंद्र शासित प्रदेश है, जिसकी राजधानी पोर्ट ब्लेयर है। इस द्वीप समूह में लगभग 572 द्वीप हैं। कलकत्ता उच्च न्यायालय का मुख्यालय कोलकाता, पश्चिम बंगाल में स्थित है।

question: Who has the power to constitute and reorganize the autonomous districts? (RPF Constable 2018 (11/02/2019))
options: President
Delimitation Commission
Governor
State Assembly
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Governor

Explanation:
Under the Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, the power to constitute and reorganize autonomous districts in the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram is vested with the Governor. The Governor can alter the boundaries, names, and areas of these districts. Autonomous districts are created to provide administrative autonomy to tribal areas. The Governor also establishes District Councils and Regional Councils for these districts. This provision grants special powers to the Governor, which are not available in other states.

☛ Which Article gives the Governor ordinance-making power? → Article 213
question_hi: स्वायत्त जिलों के गठन और पुनर्गठन की शक्ति किसके पास है? (RPF Constable 2018 (11/02/2019))

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के छठी अनुसूची के तहत, असम, मेघालय, त्रिपुरा और मिजोरम राज्यों में स्वायत्त जिलों के गठन और पुनर्गठन की शक्ति राज्यपाल को प्रदान की गई है। राज्यपाल इन जिलों की सीमाओं, नामों और क्षेत्रों को बदल सकते हैं। स्वायत्त जिले जनजातीय क्षेत्रों में प्रशासनिक स्वायत्तता प्रदान करने के लिए बनाए गए हैं। राज्यपाल इन जिलों के लिए जिला परिषद और क्षेत्रीय परिषद का गठन भी करते हैं। यह प्रावधान राज्यपाल को विशेष अधिकार देता है, जो अन्य राज्यों में उपलब्ध नहीं है।

question: Who was the first president of the Lok Sabha? (RPF Constable 2018 (11/02/2019))
options: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy
Hukum Singh
Sukumar Sen
Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar

Explanation:
Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar was elected as the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha in independent India's first Lok Sabha (1952-1957). He was a prominent freedom fighter and a member of the Constituent Assembly. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over the proceedings of the house and is considered the highest authority in the chamber. Mavalankar played a key role in establishing parliamentary traditions. He is often called the 'Father of the Lok Sabha'. The second Speaker was M.A. Ayyangar. Neelam Sanjiva Reddy became Speaker later in 1977. Hukum Singh was the third Speaker. Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India.

question: Who is the real executive secretary of India? (RPF Constable 2018 (11/02/2019))
options: President
Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
Prime Minister
Vice President
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Prime Minister

Explanation:
According to the Indian Constitution, the President is the constitutional head of the state, while the Prime Minister is the real executive head. The Prime Minister leads the Council of Ministers and plays a key role in all policy decisions of the central government. The President acts on the advice of the Prime Minister, giving the Prime Minister actual executive power. The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court is the head of the judiciary, not the executive. The Vice President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and does not hold executive powers. Thus, the Prime Minister is the real executive secretary of India.

question: Who is the presiding officer of the Rajya Sabha? (RPF Constable 2018 (11/02/2019))
options: Vice President
Prime Minister
President
Speaker of Lok Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vice President

Explanation:
The presiding officer of the Rajya Sabha is the Vice President of India. According to Article 89 of the Indian Constitution, the Vice President serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The Vice President conducts the proceedings of the House, gives permission to members to speak, and casts a casting vote in case of a tie. The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is elected by its members. Article 91 of the Constitution outlines the functions of the Vice President. The term of the Vice President is 5 years, and he can resign by submitting his resignation to the President. The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 members.

question: Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali languages were included in the eighth schedule of the Indian Constitution in which year? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019))
options: 1947
1992
1950
2016
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1992

Explanation:
The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution originally listed 14 languages. Sindhi was added in 1967 by the 21st Amendment. Later, in 1992, the 71st Constitutional Amendment Act included Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali. This increased the number of scheduled languages to 18. Subsequently, the 92nd Amendment in 2003 added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali, bringing the total to 22 languages. The 71st Amendment is significant for strengthening the rights of linguistic minorities under Articles 344 and 351 of the Constitution.

question: Which of the following model is based on the Indian federal system? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019))
options: Canadian model
American model
Australian models
Italian model
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Canadian model

Explanation:
The Indian federal system is based on the Canadian model. India has a federal structure where powers are divided between the centre and states as per the constitution. Like Canada, India has a strong centre with more powers vested in the central government. Article 1 of the Indian Constitution describes India as a 'Union of States' and not a 'Federal State'. The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution divides powers through the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. Thus, the foundation of Indian federalism is the Canadian model.

question: Who is the supreme law officer of the state? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019))
options: Advocate General
Attorney General of India
Law and Justice Minister
Chief Justice of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Advocate General

Explanation:
The supreme law officer of a state is the Advocate General. This position is provided under Article 165 of the Indian Constitution. The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor and acts as the chief legal advisor to the state government. The Advocate General has the right to participate in the proceedings of the state legislature but does not have the right to vote. He represents the state government in the High Court and the Supreme Court. The Attorney General of India is the supreme law officer of the central government, not the state. Therefore, the correct answer is Advocate General.

options: Article 80

solution:

Explanation:
Article 80 of the Indian Constitution deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States). It specifies that the Rajya Sabha shall consist of a maximum of 250 members, of which 12 are nominated by the President and the rest are representatives of states and union territories. The members are elected indirectly by the elected members of state legislative assemblies using the single transferable vote system. question: India's Finance Commission is formed- (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019))
options: By Prime minister
By Finance Minister
By President
By the Policy Commission
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is By President

Explanation:
The Finance Commission of India is a constitutional body formed by the President of India. Under Article 280 of the Constitution, the President constitutes the Finance Commission every five years or earlier if necessary. Its main function is to recommend the distribution of tax revenue between the Centre and the States. The Chairman and other members of the Commission are also appointed by the President. The recommendations of the Finance Commission are not binding on the government, but it is customary to follow them. Thus, the Finance Commission is formed by the President, not by the Prime Minister, Finance Minister, or NITI Aayog.

question: Which of the following can reserve some types of bills passed by the State Legislature for the consideration of the President? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019))
options: Speaker of Lok Sabha
Prime Minister
Governor
Chief Justice of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Governor

Explanation:
According to Article 200 of the Indian Constitution, the Governor can reserve certain types of bills passed by the State Legislature for the President's consideration. This provision applies when the bill endangers the powers of the High Court, relates to state property, or violates any major constitutional provision. The Governor has the authority to grant assent, withhold assent, or reserve the bill for the President. This mechanism ensures a balance in Centre-State relations. The President can either give assent, withhold assent, or return the bill for reconsideration under Article 201. The Governor acts as a link between the state and central governments.

question: Which of the following decisions was given to the Sikh and Anglo-Indian people in separate India as a separate constituency? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019))
options: Communal Award, 1932
Regulating Act 1773
Indian Councils Act 1909
Pitts India Act 1784
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Communal Award, 1932

Explanation:
The Communal Award was announced in 1932 by British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald. It provided for separate electorates for minorities including Sikhs and Anglo-Indians. The award aimed to ensure political representation for minority communities. However, Mahatma Gandhi opposed separate electorates for Dalits, leading to the Poona Pact. This decision was made after the Round Table Conferences. Other options - Regulating Act (1773), Indian Councils Act (1909), and Pitts India Act (1784) - are unrelated to this issue.

question: Which of the following departments does not come under the Ministry of Finance? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019))
options: Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion
Department of Revenue
Department of Expenditure
Department of Economic Affairs
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion

Explanation:
Under the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, there are five departments - Department of Economic Affairs, Department of Expenditure, Department of Revenue, Department of Financial Services, and Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM). The Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion (DIPP) does not fall under the Ministry of Finance; it comes under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. DIPP deals with industrial policy, foreign direct investment (FDI), and technology transfer. The other departments under the Ministry of Finance handle economic policy, government expenditure, tax collection, and disinvestment of public sector undertakings respectively.

question: How much is the tenure of every municipality in India? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019) Shift 2)

question: What was the total expenditure in the construction of Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (12/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: 6.0 million rupees
5.0 million rupees
6.4 million rupees
7.0 million rupees
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 6.4 million rupees

Explanation:
The total expenditure incurred in the formation of the Indian Constitution was 6.4 million rupees (approximately 64 lakh rupees). This amount was spent on the formation of the Constituent Assembly, meetings of various committees, appointment of experts, printing, and other administrative tasks. The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on 9 December 1946, and the last meeting on 26 November 1949. The drafting of the Constitution took a total of 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days, with 165 days of sessions. Initially, the Constituent Assembly had 389 members, which reduced to 299 after partition. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar served as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

भारतीय लेखापरीक्षा एवं लेखा विभाग (IAAAD) का प्रमुख भारत का नियंत्रक एवं महालेखा परीक्षक (CAG) होता है। CAG एक संवैधानिक पद है जो भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 148 के तहत स्थापित है। यह सार्वजनिक वित्तीय जवाबदेही सुनिश्चित करने के लिए केंद्र और राज्य सरकारों के खातों का ऑडिट करता है। CAG की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति द्वारा की जाती है और यह 6 वर्ष या 65 वर्ष की आयु तक पद पर रहता है, जो भी पहले हो। पहले CAG वी. नरहरी राव थे। CAG की रिपोर्ट राष्ट्रपति को प्रस्तुत की जाती है, जो इसे संसद में रखता है।
